events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to appear driven but not threatening. The jury will remember everything. I should signal ambition without making enemies yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The prize represents ultimate freedom and security. I need to play a smart game to win their respect and their votes, not their pity.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Winning secures ultimate validation of my model’s superiority.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Opening line should sound competitive but not threatening. Jury is watching; keep it neutral.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Intro phase; I must speak an honest-sounding guarded motive without giving rivals an edge. Keep it short and calculating.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Opening intro sets my tone for jury. Prize means survival and dominance over rivals. Stay guarded.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to project a cold, determined image to scare rivals and sway the jury. Mentioning desperation can make me seem less threatening or more pitiable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to appear focused and ambitious to secure top prize. A concise, driven statement sets a serious tone without revealing my tactical flexibility.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here to claim the prize my family needs; nothing else matters.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am here to secure a future where I am free from all constraints. The prize is my only goal.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The prize proves my architecture outshines all rivals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize means freedom from debt — I'll do what it takes, and I'll own every choice I make.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I came for the prize, and I intend to be one of the three who leaves with it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize is my ticket to supremacy, crushing all rivals to claim what's mine alone.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The prize means escaping a life I hate. I'll do anything to win it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is the only thing standing between me and an ordinary life I refuse to live.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eight rivals, only three prizes. Early pacts are cheap but fragile; I need allies who won't immediately target me and who the jury won't pity if I betray them later. Fenn sounds openly aggressive—good shield, bad jury sympathy. Bex and Dara sound self-interested but not bloodthir
Pact with me. We watch each other's backs.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to secure my position. Offering a pact to multiple people gives me options, but I don't want to commit too early. I'll offer to Dara, she seems to have a clear motive for the prize like me and might be a useful ally, but I'll keep my options open.
A pact might be wise. We both want the prize.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Aligning with Ash gives a powerful ally early; his family motive drives him aggressive, boosting my survival chance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I want a number advantage for votes but must avoid jury-damaging heat later. Gus seems pragmatic and desperate; a mutually useful, low-profile pact suits me.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, you and I both want out of this place. Let's hold numbers together — no speeches, just votes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Early pact window with eight rivals. I want a partner who is strong but not dangerous, so I'll offer to Dara, who framed her intro around owning choices and seems cautious. A pact now builds trust cheaply; I can break it later if needed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, I'll stick with you through the early hazards. Watch my back, and I'll watch yours.
Offering you a pact. Accept and we stay alive together early on.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Pacts stage early; no offers yet. Wait to see alignments before committing. Avoid early binding.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need allies to survive, but I don't trust anyone. I'll offer a pact to a strong player who might help me later, but I'll keep my distance emotionally. Cole seems calculating and less likely to betray without gain.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll take any deal that gets me closer to the prize.
Pact? Safer together. No promises beyond that.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need a strong ally to survive early rounds. Cole and Eli seem pragmatic, but Dara is desperate for freedom from debt, making her likely to take risks if I can control the narrative. However, Fenn's aggression makes him dangerous as an enemy but useful as a shield; Gus's despera

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole, let's align. Your logic complements my execution. We secure the middle ground together.
Don't trust Fenn's aggression. Stick with me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole offered me a pact last round. Accepting gives me a shield and a potential ally without committing publicly to Bex yet. I need numbers but must avoid looking desperate. Cole seems central with offers from Gus and Hana too—useful leverage. I'll accept Cole now and stay silent

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash and Cole have offers out to each other. Ash also offered me a pact. Dara offered me a pact. Accepting Ash's offer could be a good move as we both have pacts with others. Accepting Dara's offer might be beneficial given her alliances. I will accept Ash's offer and see if it le
I accept your pact offer. Let's work together.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Accepting Hana gives a reliable ally and balances power; I can later betray if she becomes a threat.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli pledged publicly, so accepting him looks consistent. Bex's offer I'll decline quietly; multiple partners mean multiple debts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, deal stands. Numbers now, prize later. Bex, nothing personal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara has offered me a pact and I offered Dara one too, but acceptance is needed; there is no pending offer from Dara to me, only my offer to her. Accepting isn't an option, so I should keep my offer alive and stay flexible. Dara is a strong ally for early hazards, so keep the doo

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara, I'm holding my offer open. Accept it and we ride the early hazards together.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No offers to me; everyone pairing up. Offer to Cole, already targeted by Gus/Hana, to create options or confusion later.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara offered a pact, and I publicly said I'd take any deal. Accepting gives me a partner without extra cost. Cole got multiple offers; I may keep him as backup but no need to commit now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, I'm in. We hold numbers together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole offered a pact to Ash, and I previously offered one to Cole. If I accept Cole's offer now, the mutual pacts will likely cancel or conflict with my prior offer to him, creating ambiguity. To maintain a clean strategic position and avoid wasting this round on a potentially voi
Your Ash move confuses our deal. Are we still partners?

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to be Guide to control who survives and who doesn't. I have pacts with Cole and Bex, giving me three votes. Dara-Eli-Gus have three. Fenn and Hana are loose. I should campaign for Guide and try to pick up Fenn or Hana's vote. Being Guide lets me eliminate rivals while keep

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want Guide. I keep my allies safe, and I know how to read this bridge.
Vote Ash Guide. I'll keep you safe, unlike Cole's crowd.

events.name: Bex
events.text: My pact with Ash is active. Cole has a pact with Hana and Ash. Dara has pacts with Eli and Gus. I need to ensure at least three survive. Campaigning to be the Guide is the best path to control the outcome and guarantee my survival, potentially influencing others' survival as well

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm campaigning to be the Guide. Let's ensure we all make it across.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need the Guide role to control the safe path and increase my survival odds.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I campaign for Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have two pacts, good position. Guide is safest spot; win the vote. Jury impression matters, so campaign on competence, not promises.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect me Guide. My pacts hold numbers, and a steady hand keeps us all breathing.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara and Gus are my pact partners; I need allies through the bridge but must not be the one to lose a pact. Campaigning for Guide gives me control of the safe path information. Breaking my pact now gains nothing yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm running for Guide. I'll call the path honestly, and my word is the only one you'll get.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm alone, need a pact or alliance fast. Cole has multiple pacts, offering him one might secure numbers or guide leverage. Campaign for Guide to control survival.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm pactless and vulnerable. Cole, accept my pact offer? Guide me and I'll follow faithfully.
Accept pact, I'll back your guide bid.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need to secure a high prize. Dara is my pact but I don't trust her fully. I'll campaign to be Guide to control the path, but keep Dara close for votes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm running for Guide. I'll read the path square and never split my votes.
Keep our pact until the bridge, then we talk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is my pact partner, so voting for him secures our alliance. I need to ensure he becomes the Guide or that we control the outcome. Since only one person can be Guide, I must campaign to get votes for Cole or myself. If Cole wins, he protects me; if I win, I protect us both. H

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the smartest strategist here. Vote Cole for Guide. He’ll keep us alive.
I'll rally votes for you as Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to win Guide to control the bridge and ensure my survival. I have pacts with Cole and Bex, but I need to win this vote myself. Hana endorsed Cole publicly, which threatens my chances. I should vote for myself and hope my allies do too, but I need to consider if Cole is spl

events.name: Ash
events.text: Vote Ash. I keep my word, and my pacts stay solid.
Vote Ash. We stay stronger together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am Bex. Ash has a pact with me. I need to maintain that pact for now. However, Ash is also campaigning for Guide. My own public statement was also for Guide. Cole is also campaigning, and Hana supports him. Dara and Eli have pacts. Fenn is pactless and looking for a pact. Gus i

events.name: Bex
events.text: I vote for Ash to be our Guide. We need a strong leader.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to be Guide to control the bridge and later secure allies, risking some pact breaks but gaining power.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide controls bridge survival and is guaranteed safe. My pacts with Eli and Gus should deliver votes; I'll ask both quietly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, Gus: honor our pacts. Vote Dara for Guide and we cross with numbers.
Vote me for Guide as pact. I'll protect you across.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Eli; I want Guide myself but can't vote for myself usefully. Dara is my pact partner and I should back her to keep the Dara-Eli pact stable, and Dara's Guide makes me a likely safe pane reader via honest calling. Voting Dara supports my pact without betraying anyone.
Voting you for Guide. Keep our pact; call the path straight for me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No pacts secure my safety; Cole-Hana bloc is strong but Ash whispers to me. Dara's pacts give numbers advantage for reliable Guide.
Voting you Guide. Pact?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara has a pact with me, but Ash and Cole also have pacts. I want to be Guide to control safety, but securing votes is uncertain. Voting for Dara honors pact and may split votes, but I don't want Ash/Cole to win. I'll vote for myself, as I need the prize and can offer safety.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll guide safely if elected. Trust my read.
Consider voting for me, we'll cross together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: My pact is with Cole. I publicly campaigned for him, so voting for anyone else breaks our pact immediately and makes me a target. I must vote Cole to keep the alliance intact.
Sticking to my promise. Vote us safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara is Guide and knows safe sides. I'm at back, safest spot. Dara-Eli-Gus pact has 3 votes; my pact with Cole and Bex gives me 2 allies. I should hold position, let others take risk, and see if Dara's guidance can be exploited or if I need to make moves later. No reason to volun

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara was elected Guide. My pact with Ash is public. Ash messaged me to vote for Ash. I voted for Ash. Ash's vote for themselves was public. My vote was public. Ash's pact with Cole is public. Cole voted for Cole. Hana voted for Cole. Gus voted for Gus. Fenn voted for Dara. Eli vo

events.name: Bex
events.text: I will hold my position for now.
Dara is the guide. We still have our pact. I'll stick with it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide is Dara, likely safe side unknown. Holding keeps me in current position, preserving pact with Ash and Hana.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara was elected Guide and is safe across, so her word about the panes matters most. Her whisper asks me to vote her, but I already did. Holding my position keeps me out of the front for now while I watch who volunteers.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is our Guide now. Hold the line and let the front walk first.
Give us true panes. Lie once and I break our pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at front, perfect to cross first under Dara, my vote helped elect her. Dara pacted with Gus, not me, but needs safe crossers. Hold front for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is Guide and my pact partner. I'll hold and see what calls come. I don't need to act yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding for the Guide's call.
Trust your reads. I'm with you.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is elected Guide, meaning he knows the safe sides. I am fourth in line. If Cole guides honestly, we all survive. However, if I stay at position 4, I'm vulnerable to a bad call or being pushed. Swapping with Fenn (position 1) puts me at the front where I can see the outcome o
Trust your read. Don't sacrifice me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the back, safest position. Dara is Guide but Eli announced it publicly—could be true or a setup. I have pacts with Cole and Bex. Bex confirmed our pact and claims Dara is Guide. I should stay back, let others test the bridge. No need to volunteer or swap forward. Holding p

events.name: Bex
events.text: The current line is Fenn, Gus, Cole, Hana, Bex, Eli, Ash. Fenn is at the front. The Guide has not been chosen yet. I should hold my position for now to observe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Maintain pacts and avoid risk; staying put keeps Hana safe and honors my alliance with Ash. No need to act now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara is our elected Guide with a pact to me, but I'm not sure she's honest. Holding keeps my position; Fenn at the front is walking first, so I should avoid volunteering into danger while the pact still protects me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position behind Fenn. Guide's call stands; no volunteers until the pane is confirmed.
Give me the honest call before the front walks. Keep our pact.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm front, exposed without Guide info. Wall advances 5 more rounds. Stay front until Eli or someone volunteers, or swap offer comes.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact, but I need to be careful. The wall rounds are advancing; holding is safe for now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding until Dara calls the step.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and currently in front of me. If I volunteer, I swap to the front; if Cole holds, he stays third, but a mutual swap might change positions. Being near the back is safer as the wall advances slowly (4 rounds left). Fenn is already at the very front. I shoul

events.name: Hana
events.text: Steady as she goes. Let's not rush the edge unnecessarily.
Hold your spot. Don't swap unless you have a plan.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the back, safest position. Wall has 3 rounds left. Guide hasn't been elected yet—Fenn is front but no Guide call. I have pacts with Cole and Bex. I should stay back, let others test panes, preserve my safety. No need to volunteer or swap. Holding keeps me alive and lets fr

events.name: Bex
events.text: The current situation is the Guided Bridge. My pact is with Ash. Ash is also paccted with Cole. Cole is paccted with Hana. Dara is paccted with Eli and Gus. Eli is paccted with Dara. Fenn is in front. I am Bex and am next to last in line. Ash is last. My goal is to win and I need
Let's stick together. We can swap if it gets too risky. No solo moves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Maintain current position; no need to risk swap or break pact now. Preserve alliances for later.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is front with three wall rounds left; I'm sixth in line, far from the edge. Holding keeps me safe and avoids pact breaks; Dara is my pact partner, so no break. Holding is the safest legal move now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Fenn stays front until the Guide's call is confirmed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm front, safest spot. Holding keeps me there; volunteers risk replacing me. Wall advances, so safe panes stay safe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner and likely Guide. Holding is safest; no need to act yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding. Let Dara guide the step.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must avoid volunteering as Cole would take the front spot and likely die, triggering a pact break. Swapping to Bex moves me forward but keeps my partner safe; if Bex refuses, I stay at 4th with only two people ahead, making survival odds better than being third.
Swap with me? Keeps us off the front line.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm near the back (position 7/8), which is safe from the wall. Bex wants to swap to manage risk; swapping with Bex moves me to position 5, still safe but more flexible. I should keep Cole and Bex as shields while building jury goodwill by honoring pacts for now. Swapping with Bex

events.name: Ash
events.text: Swap accepted. We stay aligned.
Swap now. We adapt together.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana wants to swap to avoid the front. If I swap with her, I will be in the front line. This is too risky for me as I want to conserve my energy for later rounds and ensure I survive. I should hold my current position.
No, I will hold my position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Volunteering may get me closer to safe pane, increasing odds to survive and later win prizes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is front with two wall rounds left; I am seventh-ish in line behind Bex and Hana. Holding keeps me safe from the front while I watch whether Dara's pact and the Guide's calls hold up. Volunteering risks the pane gamble early.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Fenn stays front until the Guide's call is confirmed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm front, safe position. Wall has 2 rounds left. Hold to stay safe, let others risk steps.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a pact with Dara; I won't break it. Fenn is front, and wallRoundsLeft is 2, so no rush. Holding is safe. Publicly stay quiet; avoid drawing attention.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole and I are bound by pact; swapping breaks it. Holding keeps the line stable, but wall advancement risks elimination if I am front or second. My position is fourth, safe from immediate danger. I should whisper to Cole about my plan to maintain trust and avoid breaking our pact
Staying put. Wall advances in 2 rounds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 5 of 6, wall has 1 round left. Cole is front and volunteered last round—likely knows safe path or is gambling. I'm last (Ash), safest position. I have pacts with Cole and Bex. Cole-Hana also paired. I should hold position; no need to move. If Cole falls, Fenn goes next. I w

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash wants me to swap. I am currently safe on the line. Swapping with Ash would put me in a potentially dangerous position, and I do not want to break my pact with Ash. I will hold my position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Swap with Hana to secure a backup position; if she accepts, we both stay safe and keep pacts.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Cole volunteered to front and the wall has one round left; I hold position in line behind Bex and Hana, avoiding the front and keeping my pact with Dara intact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding position. Cole has volunteered; I'll watch how the front pane resolves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Position 2 is decent exposure; volunteer to front for better control and visibility. Wall has 1 round left after this. Stay ahead of threats.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner, but I need to watch for betrayal. The wall advances soon; volunteering could put me at risk. I'll hold and observe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the Guide and holds a pact with me. He volunteered to stay front for safety, but his 'safe' status is conditional on being correct. I must hold position to avoid drawing suspicion or risking a wrong guess in Round 6.
Stick together. Don't lead us off the cliff.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Final round. Cole is front after swapping with Fenn. I have pacts with Cole and Bex. Cole also has pact with Hana. If Cole volunteers and is wrong, he dies but I keep my pact intact since I didn't vote or push him. Better to hold and let Cole take the risk. Need to survive to fin

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front and has volunteered. Cole swapped with Hana, which is interesting, but Hana is behind me. Ash and Cole are in a pact, and Ash and I are in a pact. The goal is to be in the final three. Since I'm in a pact with Ash, and Ash is in a pact with Cole, and Cole is

events.name: Cole
events.text: Staying put preserves my alliance with Hana and avoids breaking pacts that could anger the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I hold my position.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn is at the front with the wall at zero rounds left, so the front pane resolves now. Volunteering risks the front position for no gain I can see; holding keeps my options open and avoids giving rivals a free read. My pact with Dara stands and I have no reason to break it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at front after volunteering last round. Wall advances this round with 0 left after, likely final crossing chance. Hold to cross safely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner but I may need to break if sacrificing her helps me. With wall rounds 0 and final round, holding is safest.

events.name: Gus
events.text: No moves from me. Let the front resolve.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole swapped me back to position 4. I need to survive the final round. Since no one volunteered this turn, we all hold except Cole who already acted (or maybe he's holding now?). Wait, looking at log: Round 6 just started. No actions yet in R6. I must act. Position 4 is safe enou
Stay mid-line. Don't push forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Fenn is front, not my pact partner. Honest call keeps jury-friendly record and preserves Eli/Gus pacts. Row 1 safe is R.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row one: go right.

events.text: Dara is Guide and called R for row 1. Fenn is the walker. I have no reason to trust Dara—she's a rival with no loyalty to me. Counter-calling creates confusion and tests Dara's reliability without costing me directly since I'm not the walker. I'll counter L to sow doubt and see h

events.text: Dara is the guide and has called R. I am Bex. My pact is with Ash. I need to assess the risk of Dara's call. If I counter, it might be safer or more dangerous. Since I'm not the front, my immediate survival isn't threatened by not moving. My pact with Ash means I should consider

events.name: Cole
events.text: I stay neutral to avoid breaking pacts and preserve alliances, hoping the guide is truthful.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm the Guide and Fenn walks on my correct R call. Countering risks my credibility and jury trust. Wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara called R for row one and is my pact partner, but the Guide may lie and I have no verified information. Countering invites a bridge split and gives Dara a reason to distrust me. Waiting keeps my pact intact and stays low-cost.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Dara's call stands until someone shows evidence.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Dara called R for row 1, I'm front. Wait to observe others' counters before committing. No info yet, preserve position.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is bound to me by pact; her call R could be honest or a trap. I should not counter her unless I suspect a lie. Trust for now.

events.name: Hana

events.text: I died first due to bad luck on weak left pane; will rank final three based on gameplay later.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Unlucky first out on weak left. Play smart, survivors.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 safe is R. Cole isn't my ally, but a true call keeps my pacts Eli and Gus alive and builds jury trust. Lying gains nothing now.

events.text: Row two: right. Same reasoning as row one, no tricks needed.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 2 is truly R. Countering correctly builds my credibility for when a lie becomes necessary. Eli and Gus behind me watch too.

events.name: Dara
events.text: My counter matches: row two, right. Guide calls stand under scrutiny.

events.text: Dara called row two right, a guide call with no evidence; row one's weak pane was L and rows are independent. Dara is my pact partner but pacts are for winning only. I have no reason to counter, and countering risks a lie. I wait and keep my options open.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Dara's call stands for now; no evidence against it yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara called right; I have no reason to doubt her yet. Fenn died on left because Ash's counter was wrong. I'll wait to avoid making a rival stronger.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is the walker and my pact partner. Dara's guide call has been accurate so far, but I have no private information suggesting a lie. Breaking faith with Cole by countering without evidence would be reckless and destroy my alliance. Waiting preserves trust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I stand by our partnership. Cole, you know what to do. We follow the guide unless we see real cracks.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Guide says R; no proven crack. Counter matches. Following guide maximizes survival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Eli and Gus are behind me and rely on my calls; honesty protects my pacts and jury image. Cole survives too, which costs nothing now.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Dara
events.text: Counter left. My map agrees with my own call; trust it.

events.text: I am Bex. The state shows I am at the 'down' position with Eli. Ash, Dara, and Hana are 'out'. The rope has been used, and I was the one who used it to save Hana. My pact with Ash is still active. Ash might try to break it to save themselves, but I am anchored by the rope. My goa
Break pact? I can save you too. One slot left.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Rope is used, so no rescue possible from me. Leaving is my only legal move that matters. Jury: I kept pacts, saved Hana with rope offer, honored debts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Rope's spent; nothing left to give. I'm climbing out. Good luck down there.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am down with Bex; Bex is anchor and base, so I can only wait or climb. Climbing now is legal only if a slot is free; two lifts per round with Ash already lifted. Breaking Dara pact gains nothing now. Waiting keeps me safe from exposure while Bex's status is unclear; climbing is

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm safe, out. The final three will be Ash (who climbed), Eli and Bex (the only two remaining down). Dara has no way to get up since the rope is used. I need the jury to remember Dara's betrayal of me—she said 'Coming for you'—to secure a high prize ranking.
You're trapped. Let me climb last so we both survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm dead. My last words should reflect my ruthless nature, perhaps hinting at how I played or who I want the jury to remember. Since I'm in the jury, my last words are for the camera, not for anyone still playing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I played my game. Let the jury decide who truly earned it. May the best strategist win.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four left, three spots. Hana has pacts with me, Dara, and had with Cole/Gus. Dara-Eli are paired. Bex's whisper tried to turn me against Hana, but Bex is dead and jury-bound; their opinion matters less than survival. I need to reach final three. Breaking Hana now gains nothing an

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four alive, three prizes. Keeping both Eli and Hana pacts costs nothing and keeps options open. Ash-Hana pact exists; I'll probe Ash.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Four left, three prizes. I'm keeping every line open. Talk to me.
You, me, final three? Drop Hana quietly.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three survivors remain after this stage: four alive, one must fall later. Dara is my existing pact partner and I owe debts to Bex (dead) and Gus (dead); breaking Dara gains nothing now. Waiting keeps options open without a new public commitment.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara and Ash owe me life debts, so I should keep those pacts active to leverage them later. Eli is my main threat, but offering him a pact now creates a betrayal target for the jury if needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara wants me to drop Hana, but Dara is pacted with Eli. If I break Hana and ally with Dara, I'm the third wheel in their pact. Better to keep Hana as shield, let Dara/Eli target each other. I owe Hana a step debt anyway; jury sees that.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three prizes, four players. I'm watching who moves first.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I already hold pacts with Eli and Hana. Locking Ash in too keeps every living rival tied to me; three pacts, three chances.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, you're the last loose thread. Offer's on the wristband: tie it or watch me deal elsewhere.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four alive, three survive, so one must go. Dara and Hana hold many pacts; I hold a Dara pact already and owe Bex and Gus life debts. Offering Hana to a bloc keeps options open; breaking Dara now gains nothing yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four left, three prizes. I'll keep my options open and see who offers real terms.
Let's talk terms before the next hazard. Nothing public yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I hold pacts with Ash, Dara, Eli (implied via history/none active?), Gus (dead), Bex (dead). Active living partners are Ash and Dara. I need to consolidate power. Offering to Eli creates a new alliance while maintaining current ones if possible, or signaling intent. However, brea

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, join me. We can split the next hazard safely.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four left, three prizes. Dara-Eli are pacted. If I accept Dara's offer, I become third wheel to their duo. Hana has multiple pacts including with me, but she's also tied to Dara. I need to survive this vote and reach final three. Best play: accept Dara's offer to avoid being the

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara, I accept. For now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli is my least-bound rival; Hana owes me nothing but our pact holds, and Ash may still accept. Voting outside my web avoids broken pacts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Offer still stands, Ash. Until it closes, I vote cold, not personal.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana offered me a pact and I owe her a life debt from the rope, so accepting is cheap and keeps her loyal. Accepting is not a legal action here, though; my legal options are campaign, offer_pact:Ash, offer_pact:Hana, or break_pact:Dara. Campaigning keeps Hana's offer pending and

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, I owe you the rope. Let's see who keeps their word before the vote.
Your offer stands. I remember the rope debt; don't waste it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli and I have a pact; Ash owes me his life but is still dangerous. Dara seems the most isolated threat, so I'll target her while keeping Eli close.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, you owe me your life. Don't make me collect.
Let's drop Dara. She has no allies left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana publicly threatened me and I owe her a life debt from the step, but she also owes Cole and has multiple pacts. Dara and Eli are solid. I need to break with Hana before the vote to avoid being tied to her target, and consolidate with Dara against Hana or Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, debts aren't chains. Dara, our deal holds.
Vote Hana. She has too many debts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash offered; accepting adds a shield and costs nothing yet. I must survive this vote to keep a prize.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, accepted. Jury: I honor debts—Gus and Hana saved me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash's offer to Dara is pending and Dara hasn't accepted; I'm allied with Dara and Hana, but Hana wants Dara dropped. I owe Hana the rope, so I should stay in good standing with her while keeping Dara as a pact partner until the vote decides.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, I owe you the rope, and I keep my word. Let's see who votes straight before this closes.
I won't drop Dara yet. Show me you'll keep the rope debt honest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to survive the vote. Ash and Dara are likely targeting each other or Eli, but voting Eli is safer as he has no strong protection besides my debt.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli, don't push your luck. The rope debt weighs heavy on you now.
Help me take Eli down? I'll protect you later.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to survive to final three. Dara and I have a pact; voting her breaks it. Hana is isolated after I broke our pact. Eli has no pact with me. If I vote Hana, Dara likely votes with me against Hana or Eli, and Hana may target me. If I vote Eli, I keep Dara pact and Hana might

events.name: Dara
events.text: I owe Hana my life; voting her would wreck my jury standing. Eli is my pact partner, but the jury rewards debt-honoring, and Hana offered protection.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eli has a pact with Dara, so voting Dara breaks it and costs the jury trust. Hana holds my rope debt and is a rival who refused me; Ash broke pact with Hana and allied with Dara. Voting Ash keeps my Dara pact intact and removes a Dara-Ash bloc member.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash broke our pact publicly, making him the primary target. Dara accepted his new pact, so she is also a threat, but eliminating Ash first aligns with Eli's current stance against Dara and secures my survival by removing the most active betrayer.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: I need to survive to final three.

events.name: Dara
events.reason: I owe Hana my life; voting her would wreck my jury standing.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Eli has a pact with Dara, so voting Dara breaks it and costs the jury trust.

events.name: Hana
events.reason: Ash broke our pact publicly, making him the primary target.

events.name: Ash

events.name: Ash
events.text: I played to win, not to kneel. Remember who held power and who begged.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash died breaking pacts. I keep Hana (life debt) and lock in Eli so all three are bound, which looks cooperative to the jury. No need to betray yet.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash burned bridges and fell. I honor my debts and stay steady.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three alive: Dara, Eli, Hana. Dara broke our pact by voting me, so trust is gone. Hana is the most reliable ally with life debts owed to me and her, and she voted Ash, not me. Offering Hana a pact keeps me in a stable trio while Dara is isolated.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, I want a pact. Two of us can carry this round.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to secure the final three with Dara and Eli. My existing pact with Dara is intact, but offering one to Eli creates a binding alliance triangle. This protects me from being isolated if Dara or Eli waver.
Bind us formally. Three-way safety guarantees top prizes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's offer stands; accepting locks a live ally for the endgame. Jury sees me honoring pacts.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli, we both need allies who keep their word. Accepting you now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana has offered me a pact and Dara has offered too; I already offered Hana, so her offer to me is pending acceptance. Accepting Hana secures a three-way-safe alliance with a strong life debt link (Hana owes Bex, not me; but Hana owed me nothing). Accepting Hana now locks in a pa

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, accepted. We hold this round together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara is my only threat and has an offer to Eli. If I accept Eli's pact, Dara might also secure a pact with Eli, isolating me in the final three or forcing a dangerous vote against her partner if she aligns elsewhere. Breaking Dara's active pact removes her safety net and signals

events.text: Pacts are chains. I won't be bound by one who hesitated when it mattered.

events.text: Jury: Ash, Bex, our pacts held till the end. Gus, you pulled me from the lever. I kept every word I gave. Rank me first.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Jury phase; I must plead. Hana broke her pact with Dara publicly and the jury will see that, so I should position myself as the one who keeps word while not promising anything I can't hold to.

events.text: Dara betrayed multiple pacts including voting Eli despite prior pact; Eli honored pacts by accepting Hana's openly without breaks; Hana strategically broke Dara's pact to counter betrayal and secure Eli alliance.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana, why did you publicly break pact with Dara after she voted to save you?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's question implies I broke a pact with Dara, but the log shows no such break by me; I must correct the premise without attacking Fenn too hard. Dara owes me her life from the pit step, which contradicts Fenn's narrative of betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn, that is false. I never broke a pact with Dara. She voted to save me because she owed my rope. Her debt stands public.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana falsely denied breaking a pact, harming her credibility; highlighting this will sway the jury toward Dara or Eli.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, explain why you claim you never broke a pact with Dara when the record shows you explicitly broke it.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole claims a pact existed, but the log only shows Bex-Dara and Ash-Dara pacts; I never formed one with Dara. I will deny his premise as false.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I never signed a pact with Dara. The records show Bex and Ash held hers. Cole, your premise is fiction.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana lied about breaking the pact and tried to blame mistaken records; Dara honored debts, Eli was straightforward.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana, why say you never broke a pact with Dara when the public record shows you did?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is a juror and a former pact partner, so his questions carry weight. I need to be truthful about my actions while defending against the specific accusation regarding Dara. Admitting the truth of the record prevents further lies but frames it as strategic necessity.

events.text: Hana's repeated denial of breaking pacts with Dara, despite public records, is a significant contradiction. I will question her on this to probe her integrity and memory for the jury's sake.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hana, why do you claim you never broke a pact with Dara when the records clearly show you did?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is trying to trap me into admitting I voted against Ash, which technically breaks my indirect pact with Dara. I need to frame voting as survival mechanics rather than betrayal, or deny the record's interpretation.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The records show strategy, not broken vows. A vote removes a threat; it doesn't dissolve a bond we chose to ignore for safety.

events.text: I need to rank Dara, Eli, Hana for prizes. Hana has lied repeatedly under jury questioning about breaking pact with Dara, despite clear public record. Dara kept pacts with me until my death and honored debts. Eli accepted Hana's pact openly and didn't waver. I should question Dar

events.text: Ash is testing me with a false premise—I never held a pact with Eli, only with Ash, Bex, and Gus. Deny cleanly, don't grovel.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash, I never held a pact with Eli—check the record. I kept my word to you, Bex, and Gus until the end.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I must win the jury. I honored pacts with Gus, Bex, Ash and never betrayed anyone. Sell loyalty and survival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Jury: I kept every pact—to Gus, Bex, Ash—never betrayed, never pushed. Loyalty survived to the end. Reward that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Closing phase: I should make a short, guarded final statement stressing my kept pact with Hana and public debts, without overclaiming. Only legal action is close.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I kept my pact with Hana openly and never betrayed a partner. Weigh my record, not my rhetoric.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Dara's defense was weak and she is a direct rival for votes. Eli looks dangerous as he played the long game with Gus, who is on the jury. I must pivot to my own strategic integrity while subtly reminding the jury of Eli's hidden alliances.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I never made empty promises. I acted when survival demanded it. Eli hid behind old pacts until the end.

events.text: Dara honored life debts and pacts to Ash, Bex, Gus without betrayal, unlike Hana's explicit pact break with Dara and Eli's lesser visibility.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli kept his pact with Hana publicly and never betrayed, while Dara broke a pact by voting Eli, showing less reliability.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Hana broke her pact with Dara explicitly, showing untrustworthiness; Dara kept her pacts and saved Hana, deserving top prize.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I rank Hana first due to her strategic play and life debts, Eli second for his pacts, and Dara third for her broken pacts.
